# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Top picks**

| Need | Pick | Price | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall | Bose Ultra Open Earbuds | $199 (list $299) | Clear sound, comfortable clip-on fit, physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run. IPX4 and about 7 hours per charge, so they're weaker in heavy rain. |
| Best bone conduction | Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 | $125-$180 | Leaves your ears fully open. 12-hour battery, IP55, physical controls. The neckband can clash with long hair and winter hats. |
| Best for long or wet runs | Shokz OpenDots 2 | $200 | 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and IP57. Wired's top pick. |
| Best for running under $100 | Nothing Ear (Open) | about $99 | SoundGuys' pick for running. Strong bass for an open design and IP54. |
| Budget | Soundcore AeroFit 2 | $79.99 | IP55 and long battery life. |
| Cheapest way to try the style | JLab Flex Open | about $40 | Runner's World's budget pick. Less bass and detail, but comfortable. |

**How I'd choose**
- **Road running in traffic:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 keeps your ears the most open. RTINGS found the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz has the tougher IP55 rating and multi-device pairing.
- **Sound quality:** Bose. Runner's World notes that in Manhattan traffic you may want a bit more volume than they deliver.
- **Rain, sweat and marathon-length runs:** OpenDots 2.
- **Not sure you'll like open-ear:** JLab Flex Open or the SoundPeats PearlClip Pro (about $50, per Wired).

**Notes**
- Runner's World says Bose is releasing a new pair of open-ear earbuds within the next month. If you want the Bose, you may see a newer model or further discounts soon.
- The sources didn't give me direct product-page links, so I've linked the reviews that list current retailer prices and buy buttons (Amazon, Best Buy, REI, Walmart, Bose). Prices change often, so check the final price at checkout.
- For the AeroFit 2, Soundcore's store sells it at $129.99, or $104 with code AFSC20 via this tracked link, which earns the site a commission: https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon, which is cheaper.
- Open-ear earbuds don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you.

**Sources and where to buy**
- Runner's World, Best Open-Ear Headphones for Running (Bose, Shokz, JLab, with Amazon/Walmart links): https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/
- WIRED, Best Open Earbuds (OpenDots 2, Aeroclip, Bose, PearlClip Pro): https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/
- WIRED, Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 review: https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/
- SoundGuys, Best open-ear headphones (Nothing Ear (Open), AeroFit 2): https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/
- SoundGuys, Best workout earbuds: https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/
- RTINGS, Bose Ultra Open vs. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946

If you tell me your budget, whether you wear glasses, hats or have long hair, and whether you use an iPhone or Android, I can narrow it to one pick.
